# Webhooks API

Manage workload webhook configuration. Provider callback delivery is outside this collection.

Use [API authentication](authentication.md) for protected requests. Examples use your own resource IDs and a temporary token; saved response examples are synthetic.

| Method | Path | Operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/webhook` | [List webhooks](#op-get-v1-webhook) |
| `POST` | `/v1/webhook` | [Create webhook](#op-post-v1-webhook) |
| `GET` | `/v1/webhook/{id}` | [Get webhook](#op-get-v1-webhook-id) |
| `PUT` | `/v1/webhook/{id}` | [Update webhook](#op-put-v1-webhook-id) |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/webhook/{id}` | [Delete webhook](#op-delete-v1-webhook-id) |

## List webhooks {#op-get-v1-webhook}

`GET /v1/webhook`

Returns a paginated list of Webhook

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |
| `page` | query | no | Page number |
| `per_page` | query | no | Items per page |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request GET "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/webhook" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID"
```


### Response: HTTP 200

List of Webhook

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | array |  |
| `data[].created_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].deleted_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].external_id` | string | External ID from the provider (e.g. hook ID) |
| `data[].provider` | string |  Allowed: github, bitbucket. |
| `data[].status` | string |  Allowed: active, inactive. |
| `data[].team_id` | string |  |
| `data[].updated_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `data[].webhook_id` | string |  |
| `data[].workload_id` | string |  |
| `pagination` | object |  |
| `pagination.page` | integer | Current page number |
| `pagination.per_page` | integer | Number of items per page |
| `pagination.total` | integer | Total number of items |

Illustrative example; not a live response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "created_at": 1791072000,
      "deleted_at": 0,
      "external_id": "example",
      "provider": "github",
      "status": "active",
      "team_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
      "updated_at": 1791072000,
      "webhook_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
      "workload_id": "000000000000000000000000001"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 1,
    "total": 1
  }
}
```


## Create webhook {#op-post-v1-webhook}

`POST /v1/webhook`

Creates a new Webhook

This request changes data or starts an action. Review the target and body before sending it.

Request fields (the body contains an editable example):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `external_id` | string | no | External ID from the provider (e.g. hook ID) |
| `provider` | string | yes |  Allowed: github, bitbucket. |
| `status` | string | yes |  Allowed: active, inactive. Default: `"active"`. |
| `team_id` | string | yes |  |
| `workload_id` | string | yes |  |

Authentication: bearer token and the team header shown below.

### Parameters

| Name | Location | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Tenant-ID` | header | yes | Active team ID. Must match the tenant bound to a diagnostic token. |

### Request example

Set `ADIOS_API_URL=https://api.adios.dev`. For protected requests, set `ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ADIOS_TEAM_ID` as in the [quickstart](quickstart.md). Set any additional `ADIOS_*` variables from your own resource results.

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --request POST "$ADIOS_API_URL/v1/webhook" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADIOS_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: $ADIOS_TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
  "provider": "github",
  "status": "active",
  "team_id": "YOUR_TEAM_ID",
  "workload_id": "YOUR_WORKLOAD_ID"
}
JSON
```

Replace `YOUR_*` body placeholders before sending. The quoted heredoc keeps the JSON literal.

### Response: HTTP 201

Webhook created

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `created_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `deleted_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `external_id` | string | External ID from the provider (e.g. hook ID) |
| `provider` | string |  Allowed: github, bitbucket. |
| `status` | string |  Allowed: active, inactive. |
| `team_id` | string |  |
| `updated_at` | integer |  (Unix timestamp) |
| `webhook_id` | string |  |
| `workload_id` | string |  |

Illustrative example; not a live response:

```json
{
  "created_at": 1791072000,
  "deleted_at": 0,
  "external_id": "example",
  "provider": "github",
  "status": "active",
  "team_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
  "updated_at": 1791072000,
  "webhook_id": "000000000000000000000000001",
  "workload_id": "000000000000000000000000001"
}
```
